title: Mixture of continuation frequencies over the last two, the last one and no earlier symbols
summary: Three tallies record how often each symbol followed each ordered pair of symbols, each single symbol, and nothing at all. The next-symbol distribution mixes the three relative frequencies with fixed weights, and the weight of a context that was never seen moves to the shorter contexts.
core_idea: Predict the next symbol by a fixed-weight mixture of its relative frequency after the last two symbols, after the last symbol, and overall, all counted in context.

state.name: N3
state.meaning: N3[u, v, w] is how often w followed the ordered pair (u, v) so far.

state.name: N2
state.meaning: N2[v, w] is how often w followed v so far.

state.name: N1
state.meaning: N1[w] is how often w occurred so far.

update.name: tallies
update.latex: N3[x_{t-2}, x_{t-1}, x_t] \mathrel{+}= 1,\; N2[x_{t-1}, x_t] \mathrel{+}= 1,\; N1[x_t] \mathrel{+}= 1
update.plain: N3[x_(t-2), x_(t-1), x_t] += 1; N2[x_(t-1), x_t] += 1; N1[x_t] += 1 (each count incremented when the symbol arrives)

readout.name: mixture
readout.plain: p(w) = l3 f3(w) + l2 f2(w) + l1 f1(w); if a context total is zero its weight is added to the next shorter context

learning.description: The tallies are counted in context; nothing else changes during a sequence. The three weights are chosen once by grid search on held-out text and then fixed.
learning.few_shot_argument: A continuation seen once after a pair already gets probability at least l3; no other generalization across symbols exists.

complexity.constants_notes: Three increments per symbol and V-entry normalizations for the readout; the tallies hold V^3 + V^2 + V integers whatever the length.

prediction.statement: After one occurrence of the pair (u, v) followed by w, p(w | u, v) is at least l3 = 0.6.

capabilities.prediction: After a phrase occurs once, each of its continuations given the previous two symbols is predicted with probability at least l3.
Fails when the probe is separated from its pair by other symbols, since only the last two symbols condition the prediction.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: Recall of a pair separated from its probe by 5 filler symbols is above chance.
After one occurrence of (u, v, w), p(w | u, v) is below l3.

toy_example.description: Counting a short sequence over three symbols and mixing with l3, l2, l1 = 0.6, 0.3, 0.1.
toy_example.python:
import json
V = 3
seq = [0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1]
N3 = {}
N2 = {}
N1 = [0] * V
for t, w in enumerate(seq):
    N1[w] += 1
    if t >= 1:
        N2[(seq[t - 1], w)] = N2.get((seq[t - 1], w), 0) + 1
    if t >= 2:
        N3[(seq[t - 2], seq[t - 1], w)] = N3.get((seq[t - 2], seq[t - 1], w), 0) + 1
u, v = seq[-2], seq[-1]
l3, l2, l1 = 0.6, 0.3, 0.1
t3 = sum(N3.get((u, v, w), 0) for w in range(V))
t2 = sum(N2.get((v, w), 0) for w in range(V))
p = []
for w in range(V):
    f3 = N3.get((u, v, w), 0) / t3
    f2 = N2.get((v, w), 0) / t2
    f1 = (N1[w] + 1) / (len(seq) + V)
    p.append(round(l3 * f3 + l2 * f2 + l1 * f1, 6))
print(json.dumps({"p": p}))
